extracted.intended_audience: university technology transfer professionals, contracting officers, small business contractors, and legal advisors managing federally funded inventions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria under the Bayh-Dole Act and 37 C.F.R. Part 401 governing definitions, contractor elections, reporting, licensing, march-in rights, confidentiality, manufacturing preference, and agency procedures for inventions made under federal funding agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of subject invention
rubrics_metrics.description: "Subject invention" means any invention of the contractor conceived or first actually reduced to practice in the performance of work under a funding agreement; for a variety of plant, the date of determination (as defined in section 41(d) of the Plant Variety Protection Act) must also occur during the period of contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties ownership/reporting obligations to conception or first actual reduction to practice occurring during performance of the funded project. Separate but related non-government-funded projects may fall outside this definition (see §401.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: "Practical application" means to manufacture in the case of a composition or product, to practice in the case of a process or method, or to operate in the case of a machine or system; and, in each case, under such conditions as to establish that the invention is being utilized and that its benefits are ... available to the public on reasonable terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the statutory benchmark for whether inventions are being brought to market or otherwise made available to the public; central to evaluating contractor performance and march-in considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "made"
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "made" when used in relation to any invention means the conception or first actual reduction to practice of such invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the operative event for determining when an invention was 'made' for purposes of the statute and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of small business firm
rubrics_metrics.description: "Small business firm" means a small business concern as defined at section 2 of Pub. L. 85-536 (15 U.S.C. 632) and implementing regulations of the Administrator of the Small Business Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects statutory preferences and obligations to the SBA definition and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of nonprofit organization
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nonprofit organization" means universities and other institutions of higher education or an organization of the type described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code ... or any nonprofit scientific or educational organization qualified under a State nonprofit organization statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the class of organizations eligible to elect title under the Act and subject to nonprofit-specific obligations (e.g., royalty sharing, use of royalties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor election to retain title (§202(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each nonprofit organization or small business firm may, within a reasonable time after disclosure, elect to retain title to any subject invention, provided the funding agreement does not lawfully provide otherwise in limited circumstances (e.g., contractor not in U.S., exceptional circumstances, intelligence/counter-intelligence security, certain DOE GOCO facility programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election rights are the norm but may be restricted in statutory exceptions; elected rights remain subject to the statute's reporting, licensing, and agency oversight provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency determination and filing requirement (§202(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal agency may not exercise the rights in subsection (a) unless it first determines that at least one of the conditions in (a)(i)-(iv) exists and, except for (a)(iii), must file a copy of such determination with the Secretary of Commerce within 30 days; determinations under (a)(ii) must include an analysis, and determinations affecting small businesses must also be sent to the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes procedural transparency and documentation requirements on agencies before depriving contractors of election rights; Secretary of Commerce may advise or recommend corrective action if determinations are inconsistent with policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator authority to limit agency use of exceptions (§202(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Administrator of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy determines agencies are using clauses (i) or (ii) improperly, the Administrator may issue regulations describing situations in which agencies may not exercise those authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an administrative check to curb overbroad agency invocation of exceptions to contractor election rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller General reporting requirement (§202(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: At least once every five years the Comptroller General shall report to congressional judiciary committees on how the chapter is being implemented and other aspects of government patent policies as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic oversight/reporting mechanism to Congress on implementation and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor remedies for contrary determinations (§202(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contractor believes an agency determination is contrary to the chapter's policies or an abuse of discretion, the determination is subject to section 203(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals availability of administrative or judicial remedies (see §203 appeal procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory disclosure obligation in funding agreements (§202(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding agreements must require the contractor to disclose each subject invention to the Federal agency within a reasonable time after it becomes known to contractor personnel responsible for patent matters; the Government may receive title to any subject invention not disclosed within such time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely disclosure is mandatory; failure to disclose can result in Government title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for election to retain title (§202(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor must make a written election within two years after disclosure (or such additional time approved by the agency) whether it will retain title; if publication/on-sale/public use has started the one-year statutory U.S. patent bar, the agency may shorten the election period to no more than 60 days before the end of the statutory period; Government may receive title if contractor fails to elect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the normal election deadline (two years) and allows agency shortening to protect patent rights when statutory bars are imminent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent filing obligation when electing rights (§202(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractor electing rights agrees to file a patent application prior to any statutory bar date in the U.S. and shall thereafter file corresponding patent applications in other countries in which it wishes to retain title within reasonable times; the Government may receive title where the contractor does not file timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures filing actions follow election to protect both contractor and Government interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government license retained when contractor elects (§202(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions where the contractor elects rights, the Federal agency shall have a nonexclusive, nontransferable, irrevocable, paid-up license to practice or have practiced for or on behalf of the United States any subject invention throughout the world; the funding agreement may provide additional rights as necessary to meet treaty or other obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when title vests in contractor, the Government preserves a broad-paid up license; funding agreements may further tailor agency rights to meet obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency periodic reporting rights (§202(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agency may require periodic reporting on utilization or efforts at obtaining utilization by the contractor or its licensees/assignees; such information (and related information obtained under section 203 proceedings) shall be treated as commercial and financial information and privileged/confidential under FOIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows agencies to monitor commercialization while protecting confidential business information from public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent marking/statement obligation (§202(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. patent application is filed by or on behalf of the contractor or assignee, the contractor must include in the specification and any patent issuing thereon a statement specifying that the invention was made with Government support and that the Government has certain rights in the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves public notice of Government support and Government rights in patent documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit-specific obligations (assignment, royalties, use, small business preference) (§202(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Nonprofit contractors may not assign U.S. rights to a subject invention without agency approval except to an organization whose primary function is invention management (and assignee remains subject to same provisions); (B) contractor must share royalties with the inventor; (C) except for certain GOCO funding agreements, the balance of royalties after expenses shall be used to support scientific research or education; (D) licensing shall, except where infeasible after reasonable inquiry, be given to small business firms; (E) for GOCO facility funding agreements there are specified rules about use of royalties and licensing administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes multiple conditions on nonprofits to protect public benefit: limits on assignment, inventor royalty sharing, use of proceeds for research/education, and preference for small business licensees; GOCO facilities have special rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of sections 203 and 204 requirements (§202(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding agreements must include the requirements of sections 203 (march-in rights) and 204 (preference for U.S. industry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that funding agreements expressly incorporate march-in and U.S. manufacturing preference obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency consideration of inventor retention when contractor declines (§202(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contractor does not elect to retain title, the agency may consider and, after consultation, grant requests for retention of rights by the inventor subject to the Act and implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism for inventor retention when contractor declines, subject to statutory/regulatory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal employee coinventor transactions (§202(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Federal employee is a coinventor with a nonprofit, small business, or non-Federal inventor, the agency employing the coinventor may license or assign rights it acquires to the non-Federal party to consolidate rights or may acquire rights from the non-Federal party if the other party voluntarily enters into the transaction and no other transaction under the chapter is conditioned on such acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows agencies to consolidate rights where federal employees are coinventors to expedite development, but requires voluntary transactions and protects unrelated dealings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on agency-required third-party licensing clauses (§202(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: No funding agreement shall contain a provision allowing a Federal agency to require licensing to third parties of contractor-owned inventions that are not subject inventions unless approved by the head of the agency with a signed written justification; any such provision must state whether licensing may be required in connection with the practice of a subject invention, a specified work object, or both; authority to approve may not be delegated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts agency ability to impose third-party licensing requirements in funding agreements; requires high-level, non-delegable approval and explicit statement of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for requiring third-party licensing (§202(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall not require third-party licensing under such provisions unless the head of the agency determines use by others is necessary for the practice of a subject invention or work object and necessary to achieve practical application; determination must be on the record after opportunity for hearing; judicial review actions must be brought within 60 days of notification of determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes procedural and substantive checks before compelling third-party licensing to ensure necessity for practical application; affords hearing and prompt judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: March-in rights substantive triggers (§203(a)(1)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal agency may require the contractor, assignee, or exclusive licensee to grant nonexclusive/partially exclusive/exclusive licenses to responsible applicants (or grant such license itself) if the agency determines: (1) contractor/assignee has not taken or is not expected to take effective steps to achieve practical application in a reasonable time; (2) action is necessary to alleviate health or safety needs not reasonably satisfied; (3) action is necessary to meet public use requirements specified by Federal regulations not reasonably satisfied; (4) action is necessary because the agreement required by section 204 has not been obtained/waived or because a licensee is in breach of its agreement obtained pursuant to section 204.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the statutory grounds for agency march-in, focusing on failure to commercialize, unmet health/safety/public needs, or licensing failures/breach. March-in is remedial and may result in agency-granted licenses to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: March-in procedural rights and appeals (§203(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations under §203 are not subject to the Contract Disputes Act; administrative appeals procedures shall be established by regulation (per §206); adversely affected parties may file a petition in the U.S. Claims Court within 60 days to review the agency determination on the record; in cases under §203(a)(1) and (3), the agency’s determination is held in abeyance pending exhaustion of appeals or petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies distinct appeal routes (administrative regs and Claims Court) and temporary stays for certain march-in determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for U.S. manufacture (§204)
rubrics_metrics.description: No small business, nonprofit, or assignee who receives title may grant exclusive U.S. rights unless the grantee agrees that products embodying the invention will be manufactured substantially in the United States; agencies may waive the requirement on a showing of reasonable but unsuccessful efforts to find domestic licensees or that domestic manufacture is not commercially feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a domestic manufacture preference on exclusive licenses while allowing case-by-case waiver upon demonstrated effort or infeasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality for patent filing (§205)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies are authorized to withhold from public disclosure information disclosing any invention in which the Government owns or may own a right for a reasonable time to allow filing of a patent application; agencies shall not be required to release copies of documents that are part of a patent application filed with the USPTO or foreign patent offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits temporary withholding of invention-disclosing information to protect patent rights and treats patent application materials as non-disclosable by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of Commerce authority to issue uniform clauses/regulations (§206)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Commerce may issue regulations applicable to Federal agencies implementing sections 202–204 and shall establish standard funding agreement provisions required under this chapter; regulations and the standard funding agreement shall be subject to public comment before issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizes regulatory standardization and requires public notice-and-comment for uniform clauses implementing the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority to protect and license federally owned inventions (§207)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Federal agency is authorized to apply for, obtain, and maintain patents or other protection in the U.S. and foreign countries for inventions in which the Government owns an interest; grant nonexclusive/exclusive/partially exclusive licenses on such terms as appropriate; undertake other steps to protect/administer rights including acquiring rights voluntarily to facilitate licensing; and transfer custody/administration to another Federal agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms broad agency powers to manage, protect, license, and administer federally owned inventions and to coordinate interagency custody/administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of Commerce assistance for Govt-owned inventions (§207(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Commerce may assist Federal agencies to promote licensing/utilization of Government-owned inventions, assist in seeking protection in foreign countries (including payment of fees/costs), and consult/advice agencies as to areas of technology with commercial potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides support functions from Commerce to improve management and commercialization of government-owned inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations governing federal licensing (§208)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Commerce is authorized to promulgate regulations specifying the terms and conditions upon which any federally owned invention (other than TVA inventions) may be licensed on a nonexclusive, partially exclusive, or exclusive basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empowers Commerce to set general licensing regulations for federally owned inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for granting exclusive/partially exclusive licenses on federally owned inventions (§209(a)(1)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal agency may grant exclusive/partially exclusive licenses only if: (1) granting the license is a reasonable and necessary incentive to call forth investment needed to bring the invention to practical application or otherwise promote utilization; (2) agency finds public served by applicant's intentions/plans/ability and scope of exclusivity is not greater than necessary; (3) applicant commits to achieve practical application within a reasonable time (extendable for good cause); (4) granting license will not substantially lessen competition or violate antitrust laws; (5) for inventions covered by foreign patent applications, interests of Government or U.S. industry in foreign commerce will be enhanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets substantive, competition, and national interest tests that must be satisfied before granting exclusivity for government-owned inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacture-in-USA preference for federal licenses (§209(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal agency shall normally grant a license to use or sell a federally owned invention in the U.S. only to a licensee who agrees that products embodying the invention or produced through its use will be manufactured substantially in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels §204 and imposes a domestic manufacturing preference on agency licensing of government-owned inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business first preference for federal licenses (§209(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: First preference for granting any exclusive or partially exclusive license shall be given to small business firms having equal or greater likelihood as other applicants to bring the invention to practical application within a reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages small business participation in licensing government-owned inventions when they are equally likely to commercialize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required terms/conditions in federal licenses and termination grounds (§209(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses must include terms the agency considers appropriate, including: (1) retaining a nontransferable, irrevocable, paid-up Government license to practice worldwide; (2) requiring periodic utilization reporting (treated confidential); (3) empowering the agency to terminate licenses if the licensee fails to execute commitments to achieve practical application, breaches manufacture-in-USA agreements, fails to meet public use requirements, or is found to have violated antitrust laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives agencies tools to monitor compliance and to terminate exclusivity when public-interest conditions are unmet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and comment before granting exclusivity (§209(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: No exclusive or partially exclusive license may be granted unless public notice of the intention to grant such license has been provided at least 15 days before grant and the agency has considered comments received; exception for licenses under certain CRADAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires minimal public transparency and comment period before agency grants exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit development/marketing plan for license requests (§209(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: No federal agency shall grant any license under a patent or patent application on a federally owned invention unless the person requesting the license supplies the agency with a plan for development or marketing of the invention; such plans are treated as confidential commercial/financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures prospective licensees present a credible plan to achieve practical application; treats plans as privileged business information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence of Bayh-Dole chapter over inconsistent statutes (§210)
rubrics_metrics.description: This chapter takes precedence over other Acts requiring disposition of rights in subject inventions of small business firms or nonprofit contractors in a manner inconsistent with this chapter, including listed statutory provisions; the chapter is construed to take precedence over future Acts unless the future Act specifically cites and provides it shall take precedence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory hierarchy to protect the chapter's rules on disposition of rights; does not alter laws with respect to non-covered persons and preserves certain other Act effects as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: No antitrust immunity conferred (§211)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this chapter shall be deemed to convey to any person immunity from civil or criminal liability, or create any defenses to actions, under any antitrust law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that compliance with this chapter does not shield actors from antitrust enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for educational awards (§212)
rubrics_metrics.description: No scholarship, fellowship, training grant, or other funding agreement made primarily to an awardee for educational purposes will contain any provision giving the Federal agency any rights to inventions made by the awardee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically excludes typical educational awards from agency claims to invention rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope rule re: inventions made in performance (§401.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations apply to inventions "conceived or first actually reduced to practice in performance" of the project; inventions arising from separate, non-government-sponsored projects that fall outside the planned/committed activities and do not diminish performance generally are not subject to the regulations; challenges by agencies to contractor claims that an invention is not a subject invention are appealable (§401.11(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the boundary between government-subject inventions and independent or closely related non-government projects; disputes are subject to appeal.
